00316.label: AC · 14-day schedule

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: Individual dose / QT / hepatic review

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.note: No routine Days 2–4 dexamethasone in this NCCP AC antiemetic row

medicines.name: Olanzapine
medicines.note: Review sedation, falls, interactions and glucose

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally up to three times daily
medicines.timing: Subsequent days: duration and use to be confirmed
medicines.note: Caution with olanzapine: additive extrapyramidal effects; adjust / avoid for individual contraindications

additional_support: G-CSF is part of each dose-dense AC cycle; prescribe product and timing separately.
This AC antiemetic script is replaced at the taxane transition.

00316.label: Taxane / combination phase

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.note: Review QT, constipation and hepatic dosing; reconcile any steroid already prescribed

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg orally up to three times daily as needed
medicines.timing: Subsequent days: duration to be confirmed
medicines.note: Assess contraindications, renal function and interactions

additional_support: Fortnightly paclitaxel: dexamethasone 20 mg orally at 12 and 6 hours before treatment, OR the source IV option 30 minutes before; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV before treatment. The team selects the route / timing; do not substitute the weekly 8 mg first-dose schedule.

Growth-factor support is required for the dose-dense taxane phase. Consultant-directed steroid reduction / omission must account for reactions and interactions; if aprepitant is added, the source discusses 12 mg treatment-day dexamethasone.

00316.label: HER2-only continuation
additional_support: Routine prophylactic antiemetics and paclitaxel premedicines are not carried into this phase. Treat prior nausea / infusion reactions under an individual plan.
Continue HER2 cardiac monitoring; ending paclitaxel does not end echo surveillance.

medicines.dose: 10 mg orally up to three times daily as needed
medicines.timing: Subsequent days: duration to be confirmed
medicines.note: Assess contraindications, renal function and interactions

additional_support: First paclitaxel dose: dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV, each 30 minutes before treatment (NCCP suggested table).

From Day 8 onward: chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before treatment. Routine dexamethasone may be omitted after the first dose; prior reaction or increased risk requires consultant review.
Famotidine may be omitted under the consultant/local plan if appropriate. A prior reaction requires a separate rechallenge assessment; do not reuse the standard draft automatically.
